title: Sancristóbal 2022 · Computational EEG power model
citation: Sancristóbal et al. (2022). Slow Resting State Fluctuations Enhance Neuronal and Behavioral Responses to Looming Sounds. Brain Topography, 35(1), 121–141.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.model: Simulate 62 Ornstein–Uhlenbeck processes using channel- and frequency-band-specific resting decay and variance from positive-lag autocorrelations.
published_method.inputs: Drive looming trials with the exponential input labelled 55–70 dB SPL over 3.1 s. Use zero input for rest and compare proportional versus decay-scaled stimulus coupling.
published_method.readout: Correlate the averaged simulated response with sound intensity and compare with channel-specific resting decay. The printed dB labels alone do not resolve the numerical scaling of the drive.

stimulus_type.value: Simulated deterministic intensity input to a stochastic model.

implementation_gaps: Requires executable model integration with original fitted parameters, exact drive scaling, initialization, random seed and coupled variance adjustment.
This computational assessment has no participant trial schedule. Its source-defined benchmark requires resting EEG-derived parameters and archived numerical results.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.
